I'm Linda Kenyon. It is the final push before Tuesday's midterm elections.
NPR's Maura Laison says most analysts expect Democrats to take the House,
but control of the Senate is still up in the air.
Either Democrats will win the Senate majority or Republicans will hold on to it.
The handful of races that are going to determine the majority in the Senate are all still too
close to call. Democrats will probably pick up seats in the Senate, but it's not clear if they
will get the net for pickups they need to take control. And the states that are going to determine
that are Texas, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Iowa, and Kansas.
President Trump returns to Iowa today after Republicans urged him to restore in-person
rallies there and in the state of Kansas. The president had earlier chosen to do teller
rallies instead. Iowa Public Radio's Tom Barton reports the move comes as Republicans face
unexpectedly close races in states the president's won by large margins in 2024.
Trump plans back-to-back rallies today to boost Republican turnout in competitive
statewide races before Tuesday's election. He says Iowa Republicans asked him to return
in person after he switched to a telephone rally. The president is scheduled to speak
this afternoon in Dubuque before heading to Selena, Kansas. It's his second Iowa
visit in as many weeks in a state he last won by 13 points. Republican Ashley Henson
and Democrat Josh Turek are polling neck and neck in a race that could determine control
of the U.S. Senate. Political forecasters have also shifted three of Iowa's four congressional
races in Democrats' favor, and Democrat Rob Sand leads polling for governor. The election
comes amid concerns about rising living costs and a struggling farm economy. For NPR News,
I'm Tom Barton in Des Moines. The Supreme Court will hear arguments this week in a case
that fits the Catholic Church against taxpayer-funded school programs for all four-year-olds
in Colorado. NPR's Nina Totenberg reports. The first line of the Bill of Rights says
Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion or prohibiting
the free exercise of religion. But what happens when these two provisions clash? In this week's
case, the question is whether a taxpayer-funded program that provides pre-K schooling for all
four-year-olds in the state must include a religious group, in this case the Catholic Archdiocese of
Denver, which bars the children of gay and trans parents from the pre-K program. If the
church prevails, the next target is likely to be charter schools. Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington.
The sign-up window for the Affordable Care Act, or Obamacare, begins today and runs through January
15th in most states. Due to changes made by the current Congress, people signing up will see a
lot of changes to the health care marketplace, including expiring financial assistance.
You're listening to NPR.
Police in Sydney have become the first in Australia to begin patrols using long-arm
rifles. As Lindsay Arkley reports from Melbourne, it's part of the response to the killing of 15
people at a Jewish event almost a year ago. Police told an official inquiry that they were
outgunned on the day of the Bondi Beach shooting when both alleged shooters were armed with multiple
long-armed rifles. The police had only pistols. The government of the state of New South Wales
says a new police unit will comprise more than 200 officers who will drive specialist vehicles
and carry long-armed rifles. The government says the unit will conduct what it calls
high-visibility patrols at priority locations, major events and places of worship. Since the
Bondi attack, the New South Wales Parliament has also passed what are described as Australia's
toughest gun control laws. For NPR News, I'm Lindsay Arkley in Melbourne.
Police in Scotland are investigating former Prince Andrew's activities at the King's estate
at Balmoral with Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. Authorities say the inquiries are focusing
on victim survivors. Earlier this year, images appeared to show Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor
with Epstein during a shooting trip at the estate. In February, Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on
suspicion of misconduct in public office related to his links to Epstein. This was the first arrest
of a senior British royal in nearly four centuries. I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
